dedupe_keys.name: global single and multi hazard events and impacts from em dat and gdis 2000 to 2018

description: This dataset reclassifies EM-DAT disaster records from 2000 to 2018 into single-hazard and multi-hazard events with their impacts, using associated-hazard fields and the spatial and temporal overlap of GDIS disaster locations. Wiebke Jäger, Marleen de Ruiter, Timothy Tiggeloven and Philip Ward of the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam produced it for their 2025 NHESS paper, which finds that 35 percent of events are multi-hazard and involve 61 percent of hazards when a 50 percent spatial overlap and a three-month lag are used, and that multi-hazard events carry large shares of damages, people affected and deaths. Coverage is global, for nine hazard types. Format and access: CSV tables for several overlap and time-lag settings on Zenodo, with the Python code released separately. Licence: CC-BY-4.0 on the dataset; free. Caveats: results inherit EM-DAT reporting gaps and GDIS administrative-level locations, and shares change with the chosen thresholds; EM-DAT's own terms apply to its records. It supports multi-hazard loss and resilience analysis for infrastructure planning. Related catalogue records are EM-DAT and the GDIS geocoded disasters dataset.
